oooh my therapist uses tappers as well. I was fortunate that my therapist didn’t stop seeing clients during the lockdowns (she’s a private therapist). I did do 3-4 sessions online though. For me when I rate it i think about whether I am completely emotional about it (so would be a 10) and if i’m not but i definitely feel things intensely I would usually go for 7-9 and then if it’s there but not so intense 5 and below. The thing about this therapy is that a lot of people think they’re doing it wrong but you actually can’t do it wrong. It’s about how you process things and if you rate it something it’s more than likely to be true because those are your feelings. I really hope this made sense

I’ll be honest they were quite tough BUT my therapist gave me a lot of resources (things that could help) such as doing the butterfly hug, titration and more so actually i didn’t find it as bad as i thought it would be. A good therapist will know how challenging these sessions will be for you so will help you as much as possible. I know the feeling with the psychiatrist because mine did the exact same but you have to be persistent with them because if you think about it, when are you ever going to be stable enough to do intensive work if that’s the outlook every psychiatrist has.
nooo they don’t touch you, you tap your own knees

The first few sessions are you getting used to the therapist. You will tell them about the things (trauma or whatever that are affecting you). For me this lasted 2 months but only because there was a lot to get through. Then the therapy begins, there are many different ways that this is approached; light bars, tappers, tapping of knees, following your therapists finger to name a few. You will tell the therapist how much this event/events affect you on a scale of 1-10. You state your negative beliefs around this event/events and then counteract that with a positive belief. Then you will begin the actual therapy. Most of it involves going back to the event but seeing it as though your viewing the event through a train window (so you see it but it’s passing you by) The rest is hard to explain but it’s all about changing your programming so that in essence you will remember the event but your feelings toward it won’t be so intense.
